```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", fig.pos = "H", out.width = "95%")
```

```{r fit}
library(kableExtra)
library(ggplot2)
source("scripts/stat_method/data_modeling.R")

arm_df <- load_arm_data()
m1_1 <- fit_logistic_orr(arm_df, family = "binomial")
m1_2 <- fit_logistic_orr(arm_df, family = "quasibinomial")
m1_3 <- fit_betabinomial_orr(arm_df)
m2_obs <- fit_logmpfs(arm_df, p_source = "observed")
m2_est <- fit_logmpfs(arm_df, p_source = "estimated", n_boot = 1000)

t1_1 <- tidy_logistic(m1_1)
t1_2 <- tidy_logistic(m1_2)
t1_3 <- tidy_logistic(est = m1_3$coef, vc = m1_3$vcov)

TERM_LABELS <- c(
  "(Intercept)" = "Intercept", p = "Response probability $p_i$",
  median_age = "Median age (years)", female_prop = "Female proportion",
  tobacco_ever_prop = "Ever-smoker proportion", ECOG_0_prop = "ECOG 0 proportion",
  squamous_prop = "Squamous proportion", stage_IV_prop = "Stage IV proportion",
  first_line = "First-line", moa_chemo = "MOA: chemotherapy",
  moa_immune_checkpoint = "MOA: immune checkpoint inhibitor",
  moa_immune_other = "MOA: other immune", moa_antiangio = "MOA: anti-angiogenic",
  moa_targeted = "MOA: targeted", moa_other = "MOA: other agent",
  biomarker_matched = "Matched biomarker"
)
lab <- function(term) ifelse(term %in% names(TERM_LABELS), TERM_LABELS[term], term)

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, formatC(p, format = "e", digits = 1), sprintf("%.3f", p))
fmt_ci <- function(est, lo, hi) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", est, lo, hi)

# Ratio table: exp(estimate) with 95% CI and p-value
ratio_table <- function(tbl, ratio, lo, hi, ratio_name) {
  out <- data.frame(
    Term = lab(tbl$term),
    Estimate = sprintf("%.3f", tbl$estimate),
    SE = sprintf("%.3f", tbl$std_error),
    Ratio = fmt_ci(tbl[[ratio]], tbl[[lo]], tbl[[hi]]),
    p = fmt_p(tbl$p_value)
  )
  names(out)[4] <- ratio_name
  out
}

kbl_tex <- function(df, caption, align = c("l", rep("r", ncol(df) - 1)), ...) {
  kbl(df, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, caption = caption, row.names = FALSE,
      align = align, linesep = "", ...) %>%
    kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position"), font_size = 8.5)
}
```

# Data

Each row is one trial arm (or one non-overlapping stratum of an arm) from the
`claude_collected` sheet of `data/raw/step3_stratum_arm_variables.xlsx`:
`r nrow(arm_df)` arms from `r length(unique(arm_df$nct_id))` trials. Arms missing any
covariate or the outcome are excluded (complete cases), so each model uses fewer arms
(see the fit summaries).

```{r covariates}
cov_tbl <- data.frame(
  Symbol = c("$\\text{age}_i$", "$F_i$", "$T_i$", "$E_i$", "$S_i$", "$G_i$", "$L_i$", "$M_{i,k}$", "$B_i$"),
  Covariate = c("Median age (years)", "Female proportion", "Ever-smoker proportion",
                "ECOG 0 proportion", "Squamous proportion", "Stage IV proportion",
                "First-line (0/1)", "MOA components (0/1 each)", "Matched biomarker (0/1)"),
  Definition = c("median age", "female / $n_i$",
                 "ever / (ever + never), known smoking status only",
                 "ECOG 0 / $n_i$", "squamous / $n_i$",
                 "stage IV / stage I--IV, known stage only",
                 "1 = first-line incl.\\ maintenance; 0 = pretreated",
                 "chemo, ICI, other immune, anti-angio, targeted, other; all 0 = no active drug",
                 "1 = selected on a validated predictive biomarker for a drug in the regimen"),
  Missing = c(vapply(c("median_age", "female_prop", "tobacco_ever_prop", "ECOG_0_prop",
                       "squamous_prop", "stage_IV_prop", "first_line"),
                     function(v) sum(is.na(arm_df[[v]])), integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE),
              sum(!complete.cases(arm_df[, MOA_COLS])), sum(is.na(arm_df$biomarker_matched)))
)
kbl_tex(cov_tbl, "Covariates $\\mathbf{x}_i$ (number of arms missing each)",
        align = c("l", "l", "l", "r")) %>%
  column_spec(3, width = "7cm")
```

$\mathbf{x}_i = (\text{age}_i, F_i, T_i, E_i, S_i, G_i, L_i, M_{i,1}, \dots, M_{i,6}, B_i)^\top$;
the intercept is kept separate. $n_i$ is the arm sample size.

# Model 1: logistic models for ORR

Let $Y_i = \mathrm{round}(\text{ORR}_i \cdot n_i)$ be the number of responders in arm $i$.
All three versions share the mean model

$$
\mathrm{logit}(p_i) = \alpha_0 + \boldsymbol\alpha^\top \mathbf{x}_i ,
$$

where $p_i$ is the response probability of arm $i$ and $\exp(\alpha_k)$ is the odds ratio
of response per unit increase in covariate $k$. They differ only in the variance of $Y_i$.

**Model 1.1, binomial.** $Y_i \sim \text{Binomial}(n_i, p_i)$, with log-likelihood

$$
\ell(\alpha_0, \boldsymbol\alpha) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \Big[ Y_i \lambda_i - n_i \log\big(1 + e^{\lambda_i}\big) \Big] + \text{const},
\qquad \lambda_i = \alpha_0 + \boldsymbol\alpha^\top \mathbf{x}_i .
$$

**Model 1.2, quasibinomial.** Same mean, $\mathrm{Var}(Y_i) = \phi\, n_i p_i (1 - p_i)$.
The point estimates equal Model 1.1; every standard error is multiplied by
$\sqrt{\hat\phi}$, where $\hat\phi$ is the Pearson $\chi^2$ divided by the residual degrees of freedom.

**Model 1.3, beta-binomial.** $Y_i \mid q_i \sim \text{Binomial}(n_i, q_i)$ with
$q_i \sim \text{Beta}(p_i s, (1 - p_i) s)$, so $\mathrm{Var}(Y_i) = n_i p_i (1 - p_i)[1 + (n_i - 1)\rho]$
with $\rho = 1/(1 + s)$. Likelihood

$$
L(\alpha_0, \boldsymbol\alpha, s) = \prod_{i=1}^{N} \binom{n_i}{Y_i}
\frac{B\big(Y_i + p_i s,\ n_i - Y_i + (1 - p_i) s\big)}{B\big(p_i s,\ (1 - p_i) s\big)},
$$

maximized numerically; standard errors from the inverse Hessian.

## Fit summary

```{r m1-fit}
q <- sum(!is.na(coef(m1_1)))
ll_1 <- as.numeric(logLik(m1_1))
fit_tbl <- data.frame(
  Model = c("1.1 Binomial", "1.2 Quasibinomial", "1.3 Beta-binomial"),
  Arms = c(nobs(m1_1), nobs(m1_2), m1_3$nobs),
  Parameters = c(q, q + 1, q + 1),
  Dispersion = c(sprintf("Pearson $\\chi^2$/df = %.2f", dispersion_ratio(m1_1)),
                 sprintf("$\\hat\\phi$ = %.2f", summary(m1_2)$dispersion),
                 sprintf("$\\hat\\rho$ = %.3f", m1_3$rho)),
  logLik = c(sprintf("%.1f", ll_1), "--", sprintf("%.1f", m1_3$logLik)),
  AIC = c(sprintf("%.1f", -2 * ll_1 + 2 * q), "--",
          sprintf("%.1f", -2 * m1_3$logLik + 2 * (q + 1)))
)
kbl_tex(fit_tbl, "Model 1 fit summary")
```

The binomial variance clearly fails: the Pearson ratio is far above 1, so Model 1.1
standard errors are too small by about $\sqrt{\hat\phi}$. The beta-binomial improves the
log-likelihood by `r sprintf("%.0f", m1_3$logLik - ll_1)` units with one extra parameter.

## Coefficients

```{r m1-coef}
kbl_tex(ratio_table(t1_1, "odds_ratio", "or_ci_low", "or_ci_high", "OR (95\\% CI)"),
        "Model 1.1, binomial")
kbl_tex(ratio_table(t1_2, "odds_ratio", "or_ci_low", "or_ci_high", "OR (95\\% CI)"),
        "Model 1.2, quasibinomial")
kbl_tex(ratio_table(t1_3, "odds_ratio", "or_ci_low", "or_ci_high", "OR (95\\% CI)"),
        "Model 1.3, beta-binomial")
```

## Comparison

\newpage

```{r m1-compare, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.4, out.width = "90%", fig.cap = "Odds ratios with 95\\% CIs by model (log scale), intercept omitted."}
cmp <- rbind(
  cbind(t1_1, model = "1.1 Binomial"),
  cbind(t1_2, model = "1.2 Quasibinomial"),
  cbind(t1_3, model = "1.3 Beta-binomial")
)
cmp <- cmp[cmp$term != "(Intercept)", ]
cmp$term <- factor(gsub("\\$", "", lab(cmp$term)), levels = rev(gsub("\\$", "", lab(t1_1$term[-1]))))
cmp$model <- factor(cmp$model, levels = c("1.1 Binomial", "1.2 Quasibinomial", "1.3 Beta-binomial"))

ggplot(cmp, aes(odds_ratio, term, colour = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = or_ci_low, xmax = or_ci_high),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 0.25) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#009E73"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Odds ratio (log scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r m1-calib, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.6, fig.cap = "Observed ORR against fitted $\\hat p_i$; point size is arm size. Points should scatter around the diagonal."}
cal <- rbind(
  data.frame(model = "1.1 / 1.2 (same fit)", fitted = fitted(m1_1),
             observed = m1_1$data$responders / m1_1$data$arm_sample_size,
             n = m1_1$data$arm_sample_size),
  data.frame(model = "1.3 Beta-binomial",
             fitted = plogis(drop(model.matrix(m1_1)[, names(m1_3$coef)] %*% m1_3$coef)),
             observed = m1_1$data$responders / m1_1$data$arm_sample_size,
             n = m1_1$data$arm_sample_size)
)
ggplot(cal, aes(fitted, observed, size = n)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 5, name = "Arm size") +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~ model) +
  labs(x = "Fitted response probability", y = "Observed ORR") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
```

# Model 2: log-linear model for median PFS

Let $m_i$ be the reported median PFS (months) of arm $i$:

$$
\log m_i = \theta_0 + \theta_p p_i + \boldsymbol\theta^\top \mathbf{x}_i + \varepsilon_i,
\qquad \varepsilon_i \sim N\big(0, \sigma^2 / n_i\big),
$$

fitted by weighted least squares with weights $n_i$. $\exp(\theta_k)$ is the ratio of
median PFS per unit increase in covariate $k$. The response probability $p_i$ is not
observed and is either

* **observed:** the observed $\text{ORR}_i$ (measurement error biases $\theta_p$ toward 0), or
* **estimated:** $\hat p_i$ from Model 1.1 (two-stage); standard errors and CIs from
  `r nrow(m2_est$boot)` bootstrap resamples of arms.

## Observed ORR

```{r m2-obs}
kbl_tex(ratio_table(m2_obs$coef, "mpfs_ratio", "ratio_ci_low", "ratio_ci_high",
                    "Median ratio (95\\% CI)"),
        sprintf("Model 2 with observed ORR (%d arms, residual SE %.2f)",
                nobs(m2_obs$fit), summary(m2_obs$fit)$sigma))
```

## Estimated $\hat p_i$ (two-stage)

```{r m2-est}
kbl_tex(ratio_table(m2_est$coef, "mpfs_ratio", "ratio_boot_ci_low", "ratio_boot_ci_high",
                    "Median ratio (bootstrap 95\\% CI)"),
        sprintf("Model 2 with $\\hat p_i$ from Model 1.1 (%d arms)", nobs(m2_est$fit)))
```

$\theta_p$ is weakly identified here: $\hat p_i = \mathrm{logit}^{-1}(\hat\alpha_0 + \hat{\boldsymbol\alpha}^\top \mathbf{x}_i)$
is a function of the same $\mathbf{x}_i$ that enters Model 2, so $\theta_p$ is separated
from $\boldsymbol\theta$ only by the curvature of the logit. The wide interval for $\theta_p$
reflects this, not a weak ORR--PFS association. A joint model with latent $p_i$ informed by
the observed responders is the principled alternative.

# Notes

* ORR is reported as a proportion; $Y_i$ is reconstructed by rounding $\text{ORR}_i \cdot n_i$.
* Arms from the same trial are treated as independent. A trial-level random effect would
  account for their correlation.
* Overlapping or post-treatment subgroups (NCT01523587 mainland China subgroup,
  NCT03850444 KEYNOTE-042 China study, NCT01774721 skin-AE subgroups, NCT01038661
  maintenance-phase arms) were moved to the
  `irrelevant_arms` sheet before fitting.
